# Provider financial contracts

Contract schema v1; reviewed 2026-11-06.

These contracts are the reviewed financial rulebook for each provider source. They do not imply that every declared surface is implemented, that a user's account was connected, or that an invoice reconciled. Implemented connector coverage is listed separately. Provider-reported cost, API-equivalent value, plan context, credits and final invoices remain separate.

| Source | Launch state | Validation target | Financial basis | Reconciliation anchor |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| OpenAI Platform organization usage and costs | `first_class` / `current` | `live_verified` | `provider_reported_accrued_cost` | OpenAI Costs export or invoice-detail export for the identical organization scope and period |
| Anthropic Platform Usage and Cost Admin API | `first_class` / `current` | `live_verified` | `provider_reported_accrued_cost` | Claude Console cost export or invoice for the identical organization scope and period |
| Claude Enterprise Analytics | `contract_only` / `current` | `untested` | `provider_reported_provisional_usage_credit_cost_not_seat_bill` | Organization cost report after the applicable documented revision bounds, reconciled separately from the matching Enterprise seat invoice/contract; finality remains provisional while the revision guidance conflicts |
| Gemini CLI and Google billing evidence | `experimental` / `current` | `fixture_verified` | `api_equivalent_value_until_billing_export` | Google Cloud Billing detailed or FOCUS export for the same project/billing account and period |
| Cursor Admin API spending and usage events | `beta` / `current` | `fixture_verified` | `provider_reported_cost_beta` | Sum filtered usage-event chargedCents and reconcile to /teams/spend for the identical current cycle, then compare with invoice/export |
| GitHub Copilot AI-credit billing | `beta` / `current` | `fixture_verified` | `provider_reported_net_cost_beta` | Organization or enterprise AI-credit report reconciled to the matching billing usage summary and invoice period |

## OpenAI Platform organization usage and costs

- Contract ID: `openai-platform`
- Owner: `aibill-provider-contracts`
- Authentication: Organization Admin API key with read access to organization usage and costs
- API/version: Current Organization API reference; endpoint paths are not date-versioned
- Window: start_time inclusive and end_time exclusive for an explicitly reported Unix-second interval
- Pagination/completeness: Cursor pagination through next_page while has_more is true; query scope must remain unchanged
- Units: Usage totals are inclusive input_tokens/output_tokens; modality and cache fields are breakdowns. Cost amount.value carries its currency. GPT-5.6 Sol's $4 input, $0.40 cached input and $20 output are promotional, available until November 30, 2026 (the page used to say at least through November 21); the page names no later rate, and the rates before the promotion were $5, $0.50 and $30, so dated pricing must follow
- Currency/basis: Use the Costs API currency and amount; never derive billed money from Usage API tokens
- Freshness/revisions: Treat API results as provider-reported accrued cost/usage for the requested interval; final invoice, credits, tax, discounts and later adjustments remain separate
- Reconciliation: OpenAI Costs export or invoice-detail export for the identical organization scope and period
- Endpoints/evidence surfaces:
  - `GET /v1/organization/usage/completions`
  - `GET /v1/organization/costs`
- Implemented connector coverage:
  - `GET /v1/organization/usage/completions`
  - `GET /v1/organization/costs`
- Exclusions:
  - ChatGPT and Codex workspace seats, credits and subscription invoices
  - Prepaid credit application, tax, refunds, discounts and final cash settlement
  - Usage endpoints other than the connector's explicitly fetched surfaces

## Anthropic Platform Usage and Cost Admin API

- Contract ID: `anthropic-platform`
- Owner: `aibill-provider-contracts`
- Authentication: The implemented connector uses a Claude Console organization Admin API key, distinct from Enterprise Analytics keys; the official Usage/Cost guide also permits org:admin OAuth and eligible unscoped personal or service-account keys
- API/version: anthropic-version: 2023-06-01 is what the connector sends; the guide documents the implemented endpoints as a legacy API that remains supported and, since 2026-10-21, shows anthropic-version 2026-10-21 in its examples, whose published changes do not touch cost_report or usage_report
- Window: RFC3339 starting_at/ending_at with source-specific bucket widths; Claude Code analytics is daily
- Pagination/completeness: Follow has_more and next_page without changing the original query
- Units: Usage separates uncached input, cache creation/read, output and server tools. Cost amount is a decimal string in fractional cents.
- Currency/basis: USD fractional cents divided by 100 using decimal-safe arithmetic
- Freshness/revisions: Usage/cost data normally appears within minutes; Claude Code analytics is daily with typically one-hour freshness. Exact invoice settlement and Priority Tier cost remain outside the Cost endpoint. Anthropic labels usage_report/messages and cost_report a legacy API that remains supported, with no published sunset; the beta Usage and Cost Analytics API (anthropic-beta: analytics-usage-cost-2026-08-24) is the recommended successor, reports six-decimal cent strings with list_amount, and refreshes within about 4 hours, up to 24
- Reconciliation: Claude Console cost export or invoice for the identical organization scope and period
- Endpoints/evidence surfaces:
  - `GET /v1/organizations/usage_report/messages`
  - `GET /v1/organizations/cost_report`
  - `GET /v1/organizations/usage_report/claude_code`
  - `GET /v1/organizations/analytics/usage`
  - `GET /v1/organizations/analytics/cost`
- Implemented connector coverage:
  - `GET /v1/organizations/cost_report`
  - `GET /v1/organizations/usage_report/claude_code`
- Exclusions:
  - Priority Tier cost from the Cost endpoint
  - Claude Enterprise parent organizations and their Analytics-key-only data
  - Final invoice credits, tax, contract adjustments and payment status
  - Bedrock, Vertex and Foundry activity not returned by the named endpoints
  - Claude Platform on AWS, which does not expose the named Usage and Cost APIs
  - Claude Models on Google Cloud (Anthropic managed), where only the usage endpoint is reachable and cost must come from the Analytics API or the Console

## Claude Enterprise Analytics

- Contract ID: `anthropic-enterprise`
- Owner: `aibill-provider-contracts`
- Authentication: Analytics API key with read:analytics created by the Claude Enterprise primary owner; not interchangeable with an Admin API key
- API/version: Claude Enterprise Analytics API current reference; under anthropic-version 2026-10-21 the per-user usage and cost reports rename actor.email to actor.email_address and the activity summaries response renames summaries to data
- Window: Explicit ending_at at or before data_refreshed_at; data starts January 1, 2026. Organization cost queries start within the last 365 days and span at most 31 days. When ending_at is omitted it defaults to 31 days after starting_at or the current time, whichever is earlier, and that range can run past data_refreshed_at
- Pagination/completeness: Cursors are bound to the original filters, grouping and period; changing scope requires restarting from page one
- Units: Analytics cost amounts are decimal fractional cents; organization total is authoritative for reported usage credits and per-user rows are attribution only. Product metric objects are always present: an organization without that product's usage sees zero counts, never a null object, while an individual field inside an object can be null, which means the value is not available and must not be read as zero (distinct_skills_used_count in chat_metrics when user activity is filtered by project)
- Currency/basis: Post-discount, pre-credit USD fractional cents for reported usage credits; not the contracted Enterprise seat invoice
- Freshness/revisions: Cost/usage typically refreshes within four hours and can take up to 24 hours; engagement snapshots lag about one day. The guide permits cost/usage revisions until about seven days after calendar-month end, while endpoint references still describe about 30 days after usage. Preserve provisional status across this documentation discrepancy; data_refreshed_at does not establish finality. The four analytics cost and usage report endpoints are documented as legacy and remain supported, with the Usage and Cost Analytics API (callable with the Analytics API key) as the recommended successor
- Reconciliation: Organization cost report after the applicable documented revision bounds, reconciled separately from the matching Enterprise seat invoice/contract; finality remains provisional while the revision guidance conflicts
- Endpoints/evidence surfaces:
  - `GET /v1/organizations/analytics/cost_report`
  - `GET /v1/organizations/analytics/user_cost_report`
  - `GET /v1/organizations/analytics/usage_report`
  - `GET /v1/organizations/analytics/user_usage_report`
  - `GET /v1/organizations/analytics/summaries`
  - `GET /v1/organizations/analytics/users`
- Implemented connector coverage:
  - None; this is a reviewed target contract only.
- Exclusions:
  - Credits, tax, contract true-ups and payment settlement
  - Contracted Enterprise seat charges are not reported by Analytics usage-credit cost rows
  - Per-user rows do not include unattributable automation/API traffic
  - RBAC-group rows can overlap and must not be summed
  - Grouped cost buckets include only the top 100 groups without a remainder; their sum need not equal the organization total
  - Claude Code through Amazon Bedrock
  - Organizations with customer-managed encryption keys: lines_of_code and commit_count can be zero, pull_request_count can be under-counted, and skills started with a slash command are not counted
- Official sources:
  - [contract](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/analytics-api) — semantic `aecb6a57a18c5c93b398958a74589e7b708b80bae6eb25ceb1027208c89b9d05`; reviewed content `20d098fc6f9afab16aa3c2b6d2f7f469b54f525ca30b9834258173130e53e7a9`

## Gemini CLI and Google billing evidence

- Contract ID: `google-gemini`
- Owner: `aibill-provider-contracts`
- Authentication: Local CLI evidence needs no cloud credential; billed money requires an authorized Google Cloud Billing export or account record
- API/version: Gemini CLI session format is officially evolving; record the observed CLI version per fixture
- Window: Session timestamps for local evidence; explicit billing export usage period for cash
- Pagination/completeness: Local sessions are bounded files; Cloud Billing export completeness is established by the chosen billing account, table and period
- Units: Input, output, cached, thought, tool and total tokens where the session record supplies complete components; thought is priced as output only when the dated pricing contract supports it. gemini-2.5-pro is deprecated: effective 2026-12-01, requests to it route to Gemini 3.8 Flash and bill at Gemini 3.8 Flash rates, so dated pricing must follow
- Currency/basis: Local tokens are API-equivalent value only; Cloud Billing export currency establishes provider-reported money
- Freshness/revisions: Unknown shapes, auth modes, project hashes and token components remain missing; billing export revisions follow Google Cloud Billing; the Gemini Developer API docs moved to aistudio.google.com in late October 2026 and the HTML page is a JavaScript shell, so the Markdown mirror is the monitored page
- Reconciliation: Google Cloud Billing detailed or FOCUS export for the same project/billing account and period
- Endpoints/evidence surfaces:
  - `~/.gemini/tmp/<project_hash>/chats/**/*.json`
  - `~/.gemini/tmp/<project_hash>/chats/**/*.jsonl`
  - `Google Cloud Billing export to BigQuery`
- Implemented connector coverage:

  - `~/.gemini/tmp/<project_hash>/chats/**/*.jsonl`
- Exclusions:
  - logs.json is presence-only and never financial evidence
  - Opaque project hashes are not reversed or guessed
  - Free, subscription and pay-as-you-go auth modes are not inferred
  - Local session value is not a Google invoice

## Cursor Admin API spending and usage events

- Contract ID: `cursor-admin`
- Owner: `aibill-provider-contracts`
- Authentication: Cursor team Admin API key via HTTP Basic authentication
- API/version: Current Cursor Admin API reference; no date-version header
- Window: Team spend is the current subscription cycle; filtered events use inclusive epoch-millisecond bounds and hourly aggregation
- Pagination/completeness: One-indexed page/pageSize; complete all reported pages and prove member/event coverage for the requested scope
- Units: Use spendCents/overallSpendCents aggregates and chargedCents event details as provider fields; preserve model, kind, usage pool, Cursor Token Rate context, Max mode and token/cache splits without repricing. Paid plans in the X subscription include one weekly pool of usage for Cursor models, shared with Grok; the two monthly pools, Cursor Models and Other Models, belong only to legacy Cursor plans (Pro, Pro+, Ultra, Start and Teams Standard/Premium seats)
- Currency/basis: Provider cents divided by 100; the implemented spend aggregate remains estimated until a separate same-cycle dashboard/invoice check. Event-detail reconciliation is a separate target, and bases remain distinct: included usage (the weekly pool, or a legacy plan's Cursor Models and Other Models pools), additional usage (prepaid credit, or on-demand usage on legacy plans) and BYOK
- Freshness/revisions: Polling guidance is hourly; incomplete pagination or event/aggregate residual remains partial/missing
- Reconciliation: Sum filtered usage-event chargedCents and reconcile to /teams/spend for the identical current cycle, then compare with invoice/export
- Endpoints/evidence surfaces:
  - `POST /teams/spend`
  - `POST /teams/filtered-usage-events`
- Implemented connector coverage:
  - `POST /teams/spend`
- Exclusions:
  - Undocumented local IDE/CLI stores are not financial evidence
  - Included usage is not silently treated as incremental cash
  - Usage-pool, API list price and Cursor Token Rate terms are pricing context, not a license to reconstruct billed cost from token counts. In the X subscription, third-party models cost API list price from prepaid credit on Premium and up; Teams and Enterprise also pay the Cursor Token Rate ($0.25 per million input, output and cached tokens) on eligible third-party models only. Cursor models, Cost mode requests and third-party models whose cache-read price is strictly below $0.10 per million tokens across every pricing tier (BYOK included) are exempt. Opting in to regional data residency adds a 10% uplift
  - A fixture-only connector is not live or invoice reconciliation
  - Subscription and seat fees (X subscription: Free $0, Plus $8, Premium $30, Super $100 and Ultra $200 a month; Teams $30, $100 or $200 per seat a month; Enterprise custom), legacy seat contracts, prepaid-credit purchases, tax, credits and final invoice adjustments
- Official sources:
  - [contract](https://cursor.com/docs/account/teams/admin-api) — semantic `04d3bf84bc2e3c85d07003d4eaeb298186a2625b28069688d4e51e86d25d1c59`; reviewed content `831eb22c2dc583e1f28312c7050214603005ffbd3c041df92cbf0196b22ae829`
  - [pricing](https://cursor.com/docs/models-and-pricing) — semantic `bc2e9bb767fd34f16b1876e811af4e644955705568d8193d38ebeb61864b0369`; reviewed content `b0973c96bcd848bbac86f2a99d2daab4823fd1d10b718974feee14c1ee659af6`

## GitHub Copilot AI-credit billing

- Contract ID: `github-copilot`
- Owner: `aibill-provider-contracts`
- Authentication: Organization administrator/billing manager with read Administration permission for organization billing; enterprise billing requires read Enterprise billing permission. Use a supported fine-grained token or GitHub App token for the selected scope
- API/version: X-GitHub-Api-Version: 2026-03-10
- Window: Explicit organization/enterprise year, month and optional day; only the past 24 months are available on the AI-credit endpoint
- Pagination/completeness: AI-credit reports are period/filter scoped; seats and metrics retain their own pagination/completeness contracts
- Units: Preserve product, SKU, model, unit type, price per unit, gross/discount/net quantities and amounts; keep adoption metrics and seats separate. AI credits are the unit for metered Copilot usage in organizations and enterprises; Copilot Business and Enterprise seats contribute pooled included credits (1,900 and 3,900 per user per month), while the Copilot access plan has no included allowance and is metered from the first credit
- Currency/basis: Use provider grossAmount, discountAmount and netAmount; one AI credit is the provider billing unit and not a token
- Freshness/revisions: The current dated API version is required; preview endpoints remain subject to change and incomplete access stays missing
- Reconciliation: Organization or enterprise AI-credit report reconciled to the matching billing usage summary and invoice period
- Endpoints/evidence surfaces:
  - `GET /organizations/{org}/settings/billing/ai_credit/usage`
  - `GET /organizations/{org}/settings/billing/usage`
  - `Copilot seats and organization metrics APIs`
- Implemented connector coverage:
  - `GET /organizations/{org}/settings/billing/ai_credit/usage`
  - `Copilot seats and organization metrics APIs`
- Exclusions:
  - User-level endpoints when the organization or enterprise pays
  - Seat count and adoption metrics are not incremental AI-credit spend
  - Premium-request legacy units are not silently blended with AI credits
  - Tax, contract true-ups, credits and invoice payment settlement
  - Included-credit pools are plan context: a Copilot access organization has none, so discountAmount can be zero from the first credit
- Official sources:
  - [contract](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/billing/usage) — semantic `6a4e0c43b3cd6d412f6ca89c4d9a8b1c91699281a9d67610b365e4c490396a3c`; reviewed content `c6e469aa310c47a9a80d6287a9e1238c8abe32707f0093e14b87439c9ed2c8b8`
  - [pricing](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/concepts/billing-and-usage/organizations-and-enterprises/billing) — semantic `14f47855c7926d2e38d31f306eb7285bc248cb1b5112bbe8b66428708f20c9af`; reviewed content `9521ba0fd031ef7cffc209d02da9f9b05654bfaa8ebe0f5d7e462afe514ee98f`

## Drift behavior

The daily workflow checks required semantics and reviewed normalized-page fingerprints, records the current page hashes and runs provider structural fixtures. Each drifted official page gets its own GitHub issue, keyed by contract ID, resource kind and URL. The monitor updates that issue while the page stays drifted and closes it on the first run where the page matches its reviewed baseline again. Any official-page change is intentionally triaged by a human; the monitor never changes pricing or financial behavior automatically. Until review lands, the contract is `stale_contract` and the affected source cannot be promoted as financially verified in a new release.

Alert priority follows the resource's alert class and the strength of the change:

| Alert class | Required semantics changed or missing | Only other page content changed | Page could not be checked |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `financial_schema` (result fields of a cost or usage API that a connector validates strictly) | P0 | P1 | P1 |
| `api_contract` (default for `contract` resources) | P1 | P3 digest | P2 |
| `pricing`, `reconciliation` (defaults for those kinds) | P2 | P3 digest | P2 |

P3 changes share one digest issue instead of opening an issue per page, because documentation sites redeploy often and full-page fingerprints change far more often than reviewed claims. Every P3 page must still be reviewed and re-pinned before a release; the release gate stays red until then.
